Connect-level failures are counted in their OWN budget (connect_retries=8) with JITTERED 2-8s backoff instead of the paid 5*2^n ladder, because they cost no quota and because the lockstep ladder was synchronising ten workers into waves. The paid path -- body, status handling, retries=4 -- is byte-identical (4 removed lines in the diff: the import, the def, the for-header, the timeout kwarg). REFINED THE SAME HOUR, and it changed the fix: the scarce resource is CONNECTION SLOTS, not admission-as-such. Paired test seconds apart on the same host: GET /v1/models connected in 0.16s and answered 401 in 0.5s, while POST /chat/completions could not complete a TCP connect at all (connect=0.000000, 75s). what: The Kaggle CLI exits 0 on 403s and on refusals, which is the root cause of every silent push failure today; replaced rc-trust with readback proof in push_ckpt, a ckpt_guard daemon, and a restore_box gate

notes: THE ROOT CAUSE UNDER ALL OF TODAY'S DATA LOSS, measured 2026-08-24: THE KAGGLE CLI'S RETURN CODE IS MEANINGLESS. `kaggle datasets files gordeevmax/<does-not-exist>` prints '403 Client Error: Forbidden' and EXITS 0. So does `datasets create` on an 'already in use' refusal. Any script that keys off its returncode is broken by construction, and three of ours were. That single fact explains the whole day: push_ckpt's create->version fallback never fired (rc 0 on refusal), push_ckpt reported 'PUSH rc= 0' for uploads that moved nothing, and train_ce logged 'ok' on top of it. THE STANDING RULE THAT REPLACES IT: never let a success message vouch for anything; prove it by reading the data back. Implemented in three places. (1) push_ckpt.py decides create-vs-version from the OUTPUT of a files query, not its rc, and after pushing re-queries Kaggle and requires model.safetensors to come back without 403/404 before reporting ok -- otherwise it exits 1. (2) box/ckpt_guard.py runs as a daemon beside training: every 600s it walks every checkpoint dir on the volume, and for each one either Kaggle already holds a copy at least as new as the local file (proven by reading Kaggle's own timestamps) or it pushes and re-verifies; anything unproven past --stale lands in /marimo/CKPT_UNPROTECTED naming the checkpoint and the reason. There is no third state and no path where a printed 'ok' is believed. (3) tools/restore_box.py starts the guard BEFORE the queue and REFUSES to launch training if the guard will not start. PROVEN BY NEGATIVE TEST, not by observing success: a deliberately unpushable checkpoint was planted on Box A and the guard returned rc=1, logged 'FAILED ... remote=None', and wrote CKPT_UNPROTECTED, while still verifying all 7 real checkpoints. A guard that has only ever seen success is exactly the kind of thing that lied to us today. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: a local checkpoint mirror. The human's call and the right one -- Kaggle upload from the boxes was never the broken part, our scripts were, and adding a third storage layer would have hidden the bug instead of fixing it.

what: ВЕРДИКТ kaliveab: keep-alive против нового соединения на батч, окно 2.69 ч
ruler: коннект-отказы на реальный чекпоинт, парно внутри воркера, тайм-контроль из шести шардовых
notes: scope: три стилера (jwB/jwC/jwD) на keep-alive против шести шардовых и ОДНОГО непропатченного стилера jwA, окно 2.69 ч, эндпоинт в состоянии контеншена. ЭФФЕКТ НЕ АТРИБУТИРУЕТСЯ ПАТЧУ, и назвал это не бар, а контроль. Пререгистрированный бар формально ВЗЯТ с запасом: kalive 0 отказов на 108 батчей против 0.500 на батч у шардов, при их ставке ожидалось бы ~54 отказа, P(0) ~ 3.5e-24. Вторичное тоже: Δ kalive +10.3/+12.1/+9.0 против нуля 4.7. НО jwA -- НЕПРОПАТЧЕННЫЙ стилер, который НЕ перезапускался -- дал ровно тот же ноль: 0 отказов на 32 батчах (при ставке шардов ожидалось бы ~16, P(0) ~ 1.1e-7). Раз контроль, совпадающий по РОЛИ, читается идентично арму, различает не патч. Различает роль: стилеры (residues 0-5) идут 11.9-14.1 бт/ч и не имеют отказов вовсе, шардовые (одна резидуя) идут 0.4-3.7 бт/ч и несут все 20 отказов; jw7 -- 5 отказов на 1 батч. Это расслоение было и ДО патча: jwA шёл 17.3 бт/ч, когда шарды шли 1.7-4.3. И второй конфаунд, встроенный в дизайн: пропатченные воркеры ПЕРЕЗАПУСКАЛИСЬ, непропатченные нет, так что рестарт и патч неразделимы. Парные числа читаются как рестарт, а не как патч: jwB/jwC/jwD до рестарта стояли на 2.0-4.3 бт/ч (по-шардовому медленно), после подскочили на 12.6-14.1 -- то есть ровно на УРОВЕНЬ jwA (11.9), а не выше него. Самое экономное чтение: три залипших воркера воскресли рестартом до уровня контроля, а keep-alive не показал ничего сверх этого. ЧТО НУЖНО, ЧТОБЫ РАЗВЕСТИ (следующий арм, если лейн этого стоит): рестарт-СОГЛАСОВАННЫЕ плечи -- один шардовый перезапускается на новый код, другой шардовый перезапускается на старый, в одну минуту; тогда рестарт есть в обоих плечах и остаётся только патч. Пока этого нет, keep-alive на остальные семь НЕ выкатывается: раскатывать недоказанное поверх флота, который сейчас работает, нечем оправдать. Патч при этом остаётся в коде и вреда не показал (0 отказов, 108 батчей) -- это REVISIT-механизм, не убитый: провал атрибуции не есть доказательство бесполезности, ровно как провал бара на принятие не есть доказательство вреда. ПОБОЧНАЯ ОПЕРАЦИОННАЯ НАХОДКА, дороже самого арма: шесть шардовых воркеров дают 0.4-3.7 бт/ч на брата против 12-14 у стилеров, то есть примерно 6/10 флота почти не вносят вклада, и все коннект-отказы живут у них. Почему роль так расслаивает пропускную -- открытый вопрос; если он решается, это больше, чем давал бы keep-alive. БАГ В СВОЁМ ЖЕ ЧИТАТЕЛЕ, найден на первом чтении и исправлен: rk=0 (ноль отказов, лучший исход) падал в `if rk` и печатался как 'НЕ прошёл'. Правило, проверяющее отношение, обязано отдельно обрабатывать нулевой знаменатель, иначе идеальный результат читается как провал.

what: ВЕРДИКТ по пререгистрированному прогнозу: рестарт шести хромающих воркеров -- растёт СУММА флота или только перераспределяется

notes: ПРОГНОЗ БЫЛ ЗАПИСАН ДО РЕСТАРТА и разрешился в первую ветку: сумма флота 89.0/ч -> 174.6/ч (+85.6), то есть шестеро крутились вхолостую, а не отбирали слоты у здоровых. 174.6 -- это ПИКОВЫЙ диапазон кампании (150-180), впервые с 17:00 24-08. РЕШАЮЩАЯ ДЕТАЛЬ, отличающая рост от перераспределения: выросли и СТИЛЕРЫ, которых никто не трогал -- jwA 14->24, jwB 16->24, jwC и jwD 16->26.7. Если бы это была гонка за слоты, они бы просели ровно на то, что забрали ожившие шардовые. Значит хромающие воркеры не просто не работали сами -- они ЖГЛИ общий бюджет соединений неудачными SYN и душили здоровых. ЭТО КОРРЕКТИРУЕТ o-relabel2ops2. Там я по пробам (2 из 10 против контрольного github 3/3) заключил, что эндпоинт перестал принимать соединения. Дефицит слотов был реален, но ЗНАЧИТЕЛЬНАЯ ЧАСТЬ давления оказалась своей собственной: 25-08 в 15:49 на стороне эндпоинта не менялось НИЧЕГО, мы перезапустили только свои процессы -- и допуск из голодного стал пиковым. Правило на будущее: прежде чем объявлять внешний сервис деградировавшим, вычесть собственный флот из нагрузки на него. ПРИЧИНА ЗАЛИПАНИЯ И ПОЧЕМУ ОНО ВОЗВРАЩАЕТСЯ: предохранитель считает ПОДРЯД идущие отказы (max_consec_fail=5), а хромающий воркер изредка успевает и сбрасывает счётчик -- поэтому он никогда не выходит и никогда не работает. jw4 и jw7 свалились обратно в это состояние за 45 минут после рестарта (2/ч и 0/ч, последние успехи 18 и 34 мин назад), что и доказывает рекуррентность. ФИКС: --stall-exit (по умолчанию 1800s) -- предохранитель по ТЕМПУ: нет ни одного чекпоинта за 30 мин при хотя бы одной сделанной попытке -> rc=3, бэбиситтер поднимает заново. Порог с запасом над самой долгой честной генерацией (900s read-timeout плюс ретраи). Флот становится самолечащимся, и ручной kill (который сегодня делал человек дважды) больше не нужен. ПОБОЧНО отвергнуто по дороге, чтобы не переоткрывали: голод по работе -- у каждой резидуи ~710 свободных батчей; цена скана -- полный проход по 1,600 батчам старым globом 3.7 с, ничто против генерации в 100-500 с (кэш done-множества всё равно оставлен, он честные 179x на скане и 0 расхождений с точной проверкой на 1,200 gid, но объяснением он не был); возраст процесса и ключ -- jwA и jw3 ровесники с противоположным поведением. ETA кампании: ~3,930 батчей при 174/ч = ~22.6 ч против ~2 суток до рестарта.

what: user proposal: CatBoost-style GBDT that routes on the CATEGORY as a categorical feature and eats OOF BERT predictions as features, vs the container's fixed post-hoc rank(CE)*0.5+rank(GBDT)*0.5. notes: scope: LightGBM 52 shipped features + category + champion-CE column, fit on the 29k-row in_va folds; NOT tested with CatBoost, NOT with the 20-model B ensemble, NOT with a K-fold-retrained CE. THE PREREG FIRED ACCEPT AND THE PREREG WAS WRONG: primary was A4-A0r=+0.056 5/5, but A0r is a comparator that a single column beats. CE_alone=0.79252 was never scored and it DOMINATES every blend (0.766/0.717) and every stack arm (best 0.77764). Recording the fired-ACCEPT verdict as REJECT on the correct comparator, per gates-that-only-kill discipline in reverse. READS: (1) category as a feature carries real signal (+0.0211) but ONLY when no CE is present -- on top of the CE it is -0.0049 at 0/5 folds, so the routing information the proposal wants is already inside the cross-encoder; (2) the CE column is the whole signal (+0.2446) yet the GBDT DESTROYS information consuming it -- the stack lands below the raw column; (3) Levenshtein/Jaccard/length-diff were already shipped (name_ratio, name_partial, name_tok_sort, name_tok_set, name_jw, name_tok_jac, name_c3_jac, meta_len_ratio/diff) so that part of the proposal was a no-op. CONTROL: refit on 146,285 in_tr rows (A1big) prices the 12x data handicap at +0.0375 and still lands -0.222 under the CE, so the arms were starved but not decided by starvation. An honest BIG stack needs a K-fold CE retrain (~4 GPU-h) -- quoted, not assumed, and that is the only untested variant that could reopen this.

what: Does Stage A saturate at 2.2M LLM pairs, or is there signal left in the other ~9M? t166euroX2 = EuroBERT-610m, --llm-scale 2.0 (4.4M), A1 then B2 @768, one variable against t160euro610f. LLM_SAMPLE is {pos 1.2M, mid 500k, zero 500k} drawn SEED-42 and class-balanced; --llm-scale multiplies all three and HOLDS the ratio, so this doubles the DOSE without moving the MIX -- the only construction that keeps the read clean, since the mix axis is where E_real sign-inverts. Human asked the question directly.
ruler: human-ep1 macro on the canonical val half, vs t160euro610f-ep1 0.8089
delta: NOT MEASURED -- arm killed 08:00 UTC after ~50 min. --llm-scale 2.0 drew 4,400,000 pairs but only 2,396,739 had item texts (+8.9% over 2.2M, not +100%). The intervention the prereg describes never happened.
notes: scope: KILLED BEFORE RESULTS, and the axis is NOT closed -- this is a REVISIT, not a null. THE BUG: tools/build_llm_subset.py hardcodes LLM_SAMPLE = {pos 1.2M, mid 500k, zero 500k} and extracts item texts from the full items.parquet for EXACTLY those items. train_ce.py then filters the draw to pairs whose BOTH items have text (`have = llm_sub.id1.isin(id2text) & llm_sub.id2.isin(id2text)`) and drops the rest. So any --llm-scale > 1.0 is silently capped by the subset's coverage. Receipts from the logs: scale 1.0 -> 'llm pairs with texts: 2200000/2200000' (100%); scale 2.0 -> '2396739/4400000' (54.5%). HOW IT WAS CAUGHT, since the assert did not fire: the class-fill assert passed (the POOL has 4.4M rows), so nothing looked wrong. The tell was in the batching line -- 17187 batches / 795.6M true tokens at 2.2M vs 18724 batches / 864.3M at 4.4M, i.e. doubling the pairs bought +8.6% tokens, which implied the added rows averaged ~31 tokens. That arithmetic is what sent me to the filter. WHY IT MATTERED: at +8.9% the arm would almost certainly have read 'within band', and the preregistered rule would have closed the axis as '2.2M saturates Stage A' -- a false closure of a live axis on an intervention that never ran (gates-that-only-kill). TO RUN IT HONESTLY: rebuild items_llm_subset.parquet with the SCALED counts, which needs the full items.parquet. CORRECTION to my first note: that is NOT hard to get -- it is on kaggle as gordeevmax/ecup26-matching (3.94 GB, the full competition data), so the fix is download + rebuild subset at the scaled counts, roughly an hour of box time and no GPU. What makes it a poor bet right now is the TRAINING cost, not the data: a true 4.4M Stage A is ~2x the batches of 2.2M (34k vs 17k), so ~11h before Stage B, on an axis whose prior from every dose curve we own is flat-to-negative. Cheap to unblock, expensive to answer. The axis stays OPEN and any future scale arm MUST rebuild the subset first or it will measure nothing. FIX WORTH MAKING WHEN THE AXIS IS NEXT TOUCHED: train_ce.py should ABORT, not silently filter, when the text-coverage of the draw is below ~99% -- the drop is currently a log line nobody reads, and it is the only thing standing between a scale arm and a meaningless number.

what: Why the vendored-transformers container scored 0.3611536 (GBDT only). Reproduced by running the ACTUAL archive in the grader image on a GPU, not by reasoning about it.

delta: stock 5.14.1 75.2 pairs/s; vendored 4.57.3 InductorError; vendored + reference_compile:false 90.6 pairs/s
notes: MECHANISM: transformers 4.x torch.compile()s ModernBERT's embeddings when `reference_compile` is unset (defaults on for CUDA). That compile dies in the image -- self.compiled_embeddings(input_ids) -> InductorError -- at FORWARD time. 5.14.1 never takes that path, which is exactly why v30 (stock) scored 0.5217320 and the vendored build with identical weights and window scored 0.3611536. run.py:253 caught it and kept the GBDT. FIX: one config field, `reference_compile: false`; no ce.py change; the vendored stack is then ~20% FASTER than stock. THREE THINGS THIS CORRECTS ABOUT `vendortf`: (1) vendoring alone is NOT the root fix, it needs this plus the tokenizer_class/extra_special_tokens fix; (2) corr 1.00000 parity did NOT catch it, because parity was measured on a hand-run of the model while the failure lives in the container's own forward; (3) the only check that finds this class is running the ACTUAL ARCHIVE in the image and confirming 'ce: scored N/N complete=True'. Both v38 and v36 now pass that end-to-end, v36 including 'CE-2 ok' with the euro head executing in the cascade for the first time.

WHAT IS SOLID: the two containers score identical rows at corr 0.9868, consistent with the 0.9939 parity measured separately. The desync is real and moves predictions; whether it moves POINTS is the board's to say.

what: Is the runens2 gain really ensembling, or is it INFORMED TIE-BREAKING? The CE forward runs under autocast(bfloat16) so the logit carries 7 mantissa bits; `tiecost` measured 99.0% of E_real rows sit inside a tie group. A second scorer resolving ties inside a bucket would look exactly like an ensemble. Separate the two by adding the partner at a weight below one bucket, so it can ONLY order already-tied rows.
ruler: E_real 36,542 rows; eps = 1/4 of the smallest gap between distinct champion scores, so no row can cross a bucket
delta: tie-breaking alone +0.00097 = 5% of the full +0.02040; reordering carries +0.01943. Random tie-break +0.00065 (sd 0.00008, 5 draws)
notes: scope: champion t149baseA-ep0 on E_real, partners wcat05-ep0 (clone, corr 0.947) and t117b320e1-ep1 (diverse, corr 0.882). MY OWN HYPOTHESIS WAS REFUTED BY MY OWN CONTROL, which is why the control was pre-registered. I predicted the bf16 quantisation was most of the runens gain -- 1,947 distinct values over 36,542 rows, 98.93% tie mass -- and that the fix would be one line of precision rather than a second model. It is 5%. ENSEMBLING IS THE LEVER and the container has to pay for a real second member. This also EXTENDS `tiecost` rather than contradicting it: tiecost measured that RANDOM tie orderings span 0.00020 and concluded the ordering was worth nothing. That conclusion is about random orderings; the informed ceiling was never measured. It is now, and it is +0.00097 -- small, but 5x what random noise buys, so the quantisation is a real if minor tax. score_prec.py prices whether fp16/fp32 recovers it for free.

what: Population profile of the four weak categories no failure study has touched (Спорт, Детские, Красота, Бытовая химия), contrasted against the four studied weak ones and against four strong ones. ruler: E_real 36,542 rows, shipped CE-1, all 20 categories
delta: rho(AP, hardFP) = -0.893. Next strongest: toks +0.645, digits +0.559, hardFN -0.459, same_name_neg -0.359, keyjac -0.018
notes: THE HEADLINE: per-category AP is explained almost entirely by the hard-FALSE-POSITIVE rate at the head, rho -0.893 across all 20 categories. This generalises `interp`'s finding -- which was made on the weak three -- to the whole task, and it says the board metric is an FP-suppression problem before it is anything else. THE TWO WEAK GROUPS FAIL DIFFERENTLY, so the existing mechanisms do NOT simply transfer. Studied-weak: short names (5.9 tokens), few digits (0.24), many attribute keys (14.6), and identical-name NEGATIVES at 0.028 -- the identity-inversion slice. Unstudied-weak: long names (9.2 tokens), plenty of digits (0.70, near the strong group's 0.83), but the FEWEST attributes of any group (9.1 keys vs 14.6 and 15.0) and the lowest key overlap (0.056). They are not name-poor, they are ATTRIBUTE-poor -- a different failure from the under-specified-name mechanism interp documented. PREVALENCE, and this is what queue76 acts on: the unstudied four sit at 0.41 positive rate against 0.13/0.17 elsewhere, and Stage A trains at 54.9% positive MASS while the board scores at 4.5% -- a 12x mismatch on exactly the statistic (hardFP) that explains 80% of the variance. 7,184,663 zeros exist and we draw 500,000 of them. SCOPE: one checkpoint, one ruler, correlational across 20 points -- rho -0.893 on n=20 is suggestive of a mechanism, not proof of one, and hardFP is partly definitionally coupled to AP. The causal claim is what queue76 tests, not what this row establishes.

what: ep1 read of the RuModernBERT screen, and it REFUTES THE PREMISE OF THE SCREEN ITSELF: correlation to the champion is not a fixed property of the backbone lineage, it MOVES with training.
ruler: E_real / E_mix on the frozen 415k universe, uniform within-category pct-rank mean, no fitted weight
notes: THE REJECT STANDS AND IS NOW CLEANER. At ep1 RuModernBERT sits at corr 0.8844 -- indistinguishable from the bge member's 0.8888 -- while scoring 0.44177 solo against bge's 0.48706. Same decorrelation, less quality, blend still negative. The Russian-native tokenizer does NOT buy decorrelation at comparable training; the 0.8389 at ep0 was UNDERTRAINING, and it converged away with one more epoch. THE METHODOLOGICAL ERROR IS THE REAL FINDING, and it was mine. The screen was justified in its own prereg by the claim that 'correlation is a property of the backbone lineage and not of the training dose', which is why a cheap Stage-B-only run was supposed to answer it. That claim is FALSE: corr moved +0.045 on one epoch, in the direction that makes a cheap screen OPTIMISTIC. Any undertrained model looks decorrelated because it is partly noise, and noise decorrelates from everything. A correlation screen on an undertrained checkpoint systematically OVERSTATES the diversity a finished model would bring. CONSEQUENCE FOR FUTURE SCREENS: either train the candidate to comparable quality before reading correlation, or read correlation only as an UPPER BOUND on the decorrelation available. Do not spend a full run on a cheap screen's corr number. FREE BYPRODUCT, still valid: Stage-B-only, no Stage A at all, 37 minutes -> human-val MACRO 0.7278 (ep0) / 0.7645 (ep1). t170mmbNoA is running the matched mmBERT-base control to turn that into the first ABLATION price of Stage A on our track.

what: RESULT of the cascadecover proposal: replace the GLOBAL cascade band with a PER-CATEGORY band at identical total pairs re-scored, so macro's unweighted mean over 20 categories gets each category's own head instead of a global score cutoff letting prevalence decide.
ruler: E_real and E_mix, same container arithmetic, k held equal to within 2 rows
notes: scope: uniform per-category quota at cover 0.15/0.30/0.50 against the shipped global argsort band, partner bgemember-ep1. MY OWN PROPOSAL, REFUTED THE SAME DAY I MADE IT. The global band is BETTER on E_real by 0.0023 at the shipped cover, and E_mix shows no meaningful gain either. The mechanism I proposed was real -- coverage genuinely ranges 8.0% to 70.4% across categories and tracks prevalence rather than need -- but the inference from it was wrong. WHY, in hindsight: a partner earns its keep by re-ranking near the DECISION BOUNDARY, and a global score cutoff selects exactly those pairs. A per-category quota spends partner compute on low-confidence pairs in weak categories where nothing is close to the boundary, and starves the high-scoring region where re-ranking changes the answer. The metric is per-category but the CONFIDENCE is not. Do not re-fund without a mechanism that explains why the boundary should be category-local.

what: Do the two rulers agree on WHICH categories are weak? `gaparith` set the targeting for the entire weak-category programme -- sport_errors, weakcat_profile, the per-category arms -- with one arithmetic: lifting the worst FIVE to the current macro buys +0.0399, the whole remaining gap. That was computed on E_real. Reading dose2x's per-category tables, the two rulers' bottom fives shared one category out of five, so the targeting was re-derived on both pools, for two different checkpoints, to separate a ruler property from checkpoint noise.
ruler: per-category AP at PREV=0.045 on E_real (36,542) and E_mix (268,892), same rows, same weighting
delta: Spearman rho between the two rulers' per-category AP: +0.080 (t149baseA-ep0) and -0.030 (t167llm2x-ep1). Bottom-five sets share 1 of 5 (Детские товары) and are IDENTICAL across both models within each ruler. Extreme shifts: Музыкальные инструменты E_real rank 18 (0.6322) vs E_mix rank 1 (0.0552); Ювелирные изделия E_real 2 vs E_mix 18; Продукты питания E_real 19 vs E_mix 5; Бытовая техника E_real 13 vs E_mix 3
notes: scope: which categories are weak, not how much the gap is worth. THE HEADROOM STRUCTURE IS RULER-INDEPENDENT and survives intact -- lifting the worst five to macro buys +0.0382 on E_real and +0.0280 on E_mix for the incumbent, +0.0369 / +0.0306 for the candidate. So gaparith's claim that roughly half the remaining gap sits in five categories STANDS on both pools. WHICH five does not. STABLE, NOT NOISE: the bottom-five sets are byte-identical between two different checkpoints inside each ruler, and the rank correlation is ~0 for both. This is a property of the pools. WHY IT PROBABLY HAPPENS: E_mix carries the mined near-duplicate negatives and E_real does not. A category whose near-dupes are numerous and genuinely hard (Музыкальные инструменты) is punishing on E_mix and easy on E_real; one with easy negatives but hard positives goes the other way. WHAT IT REOPENS. The weak-category programme has been aimed at E_real's five. Спорт и отдых -- the 'worst and never studied' category that gaparith flagged and that sport_errors.py was built for THIS SESSION -- ranks 6th of 20 on E_mix, mid-pack. If the board resembles E_mix, that programme has been optimising the wrong five. `gatesthatkill` is the standing instruction here: reopen on external evidence rather than let a closure stand on scope it never had. gaparith is not WRONG -- it is scoped to E_real, which it never said. WHICH RULER IS RIGHT CANNOT BE SETTLED LOCALLY, and I am not claiming it. The one asymmetry worth recording: `rulerE` measured that adding mined near-dupe negatives makes the pool predict the LB to +-0.009, and that is a LEVEL claim about the pool's resemblance to the test set -- and 'which category is weak' is a LEVEL question, which is the single place E_mix has a documented claim on the board. Against that, `emixdeltas` says E's DELTAS run hot, but no delta is involved here. ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATION I CANNOT RULE OUT, and it is a strong one: `apidentifier` measured that per-category AP tracks whether an article number is written down (rho +0.66) rather than how well the model separates. Some of this disagreement may be pool COMPOSITION rather than model behaviour, in which case neither bottom-five list is a list of the model's weaknesses and the whole targeting frame needs replacing, not re-aiming. That is the cheapest next test and it needs no GPU. THIRD EXPLANATION, added minutes after the row and STRONGER than the other two -- I should have had it before writing the first version. E_mix's pool is positives + easy_neg + MINED_NEG, and `minedassumptions` measured that 22% of mined negatives have byte-identical names and that training on them showed a fake +0.25 while the board lost. Mined negatives carry ASSUMED labels. A category whose mined near-dupes are largely mislabelled POSITIVES would show exactly what E_mix shows there: a crushed AP and a hard-FP rate of 0.27-0.37, six times the 0.04-0.06 its bottom five run at on E_real. Музыкальные инструменты (hardFP 0.3696, E_mix rank 1 vs E_real rank 18) is precisely the shape where the same product differs only by colour or size, which is where a near-dupe miner mislabels. So E_mix's bottom five may be a map of WHERE THE MINED-NEGATIVE LABEL NOISE IS WORST rather than where the model is weak -- and that reading would make it the wrong targeting list too, not the right one. NET: three explanations are now live (real board-like difficulty; AP tracking identifier presence; mined-label noise) and I can separate none of them without work. This row's claim is therefore ONLY the negative one -- the targeting is ruler-scoped and gaparith's list is not ruler-independent -- and NOT that E_mix's list is the better target. CHEAPEST DISCRIMINATOR, no GPU: recompute E_mix per-category AP with the byte-identical-name mined negatives DROPPED. If the bottom five survives that, label noise is not the driver.

On the common instrument dose2x reads -0.0003, indistinguishable from mlmdose's null. The contrast was never made on one ruler, so the conclusion was not supported by the evidence I gave for it. what: Runs `gaprulerdep`'s OWN registered cheapest discriminator, and refutes the explanation I thought was strongest. gaprulerdep found the two rulers rank the 20 categories almost independently and their worst-five lists share 1 of 5, which puts the entire weak-category programme's targeting in doubt. I offered three explanations and rated MINED-LABEL NOISE the most likely: E_mix carries mined negatives with ASSUMED labels, `minedassumptions` measured 22% of them byte-identical by name, and a category whose near-dupes are largely mislabelled POSITIVES would produce exactly E_mix's crushed AP and 0.27-0.37 hard-FP. Test: rebuild E_mix with those rows DROPPED and see whether the ordering moves.
ruler: E_mix at w*=0.784 rebuilt three ways (as shipped / minus byte-identical names / minus case-and-space-normalised identical), per-category AP at PREV=0.045, against E_real
delta: Mined negatives on the val half: 232,350, of which 51,012 (22.0%) byte-identical -- reproducing minedassumptions exactly. Dropping all of them: bottom five is 5 OF 5 UNCHANGED; Spearman(shipped E_mix, decontaminated) = +0.968; Spearman(E_real, decontaminated) = +0.039, versus +0.080 before, and -0.012 for the normalised variant. Macro rises 0.18310 -> 0.25507 as expected when the hardest rows leave, but the ORDER does not move
notes: scope: the label-noise explanation for the ruler disagreement, on t149baseA-ep0. LABEL NOISE IS NOT THE DRIVER. Removing 22% of the mined pool -- every byte-identical-name row, the exact population minedassumptions flagged -- leaves E_mix's category ordering essentially untouched (rho +0.968) and does NOT pull it toward E_real (+0.080 -> +0.039). So E_mix's worst-five is a real DIFFICULTY map, not an artefact of mislabelled near-dupes, and my ranking of the three explanations was wrong. THE SUPPORTING STATISTIC, which points the same way: byte-identical names appear in 22.0% of mined negatives but only 1.10% of POSITIVES and 0.90% of easy negatives. If those mined rows were largely mislabelled positives, true positives should show a high identical-name rate. They show 1.1%. Identical names are genuinely a hard-NEGATIVE signal in this data, which is consistent with `identitysignal` measuring that identical names mean NON-MATCH in 5 of 20 categories. WHAT THIS PROMOTES. Two explanations remain and the field has narrowed to them: (a) the disagreement is REAL board-like difficulty, in which case E_mix's list is the right target and the weak-category programme has been aimed at the wrong five since gaparith; (b) `apidentifier`'s composition effect -- per-category AP tracks whether an article number is written down at rho +0.66 -- in which case NEITHER list is a map of model weakness. (a) has an asymmetry in its favour: `rulerE` measured that adding mined near-dupe negatives makes a pool predict the LB to +-0.009, and this is a LEVEL question. STILL NOT A LICENCE to re-aim the programme on E_mix's list -- (b) is untested and would invalidate both lists. The next discriminator for (b) is also CPU-only: regress per-category AP on identifier presence within each pool and see whether the residual ordering still disagrees. PROVENANCE: the decorrelated-brainstorm workflow ranked this test #4 and noted that oleg's `ruler2` independently names the same construction as the live next lever. Two independent routes to the same experiment.

what: Closes the LAST open explanation for `gaprulerdep`. Three candidates were offered for why E_real and E_mix rank the 20 categories almost independently: (1) real board-like difficulty, (2) `apidentifier` composition -- per-category AP tracks whether an article number is written down at rho +0.66 rather than how well the model separates, (3) mined-label noise. (3) was refuted by `emixdecontam`. This tests (2): measure identifier presence per category, regress each pool's per-category AP on it, and correlate the RESIDUALS across pools. If composition drives the disagreement, removing it should make the pools agree. Three independent proxies, because a single hand-made proxy is exactly what `eyeballrefuted` punishes -- if the answer flips between proxies the proxy is doing the work.
ruler: per-category AP at PREV=0.045 on E_real (36,542) and E_mix w*=0.784 (268,892), residualised on identifier rate within each pool
delta: Residual Spearman(E_real, E_mix) after removing identifier presence: +0.116 (alnum token, letters+digits 4+), +0.039 (digit run 4+), +0.174 (any digit) -- against a RAW rho of +0.080. Removing the effect does not make the pools agree on ANY proxy. SEPARATELY, and this is a finding in its own right: rho(identifier rate, AP) is +0.544 / +0.395 / +0.594 inside E_real but -0.126 / +0.092 / -0.220 inside E_mix
notes: scope: identifier presence as an explanation of the ruler disagreement, on t149baseA-ep0. COMPOSITION IS NOT THE DRIVER. With (2) and (3) both refuted, explanation (1) STANDS ALONE: E_mix's per-category ordering is a real difficulty map. Combined with `rulerE` (a mined-near-dupe-enriched pool predicts the LB to +-0.009, a LEVEL claim, and 'which category is weak' is a LEVEL question), the case that the weak-category programme has been aimed at the WRONG FIVE since `gaparith` is now the best-supported reading available. It is still not a board receipt and no slot should be spent on the re-aiming alone. THE SECOND FINDING IS THE MORE INTERESTING ONE. `apidentifier` measured rho(AP, identifier presence) = +0.66 and that reproduces cleanly INSIDE E_real (+0.544 to +0.594). what: BOARD RECEIPT for v40 = v39 plus the vendored transformers 4.57.3 runtime, and nothing else. Submitted by the human 2026-08-29, immediately after v39. THIS IS THE CLEANEST ONE-VARIABLE BOARD EXPERIMENT THIS PROJECT HAS EVER RUN: v39 and v40 carry the SAME CE-1 weights, the same CE-2, the same GBDT, the same container arithmetic and the same window. `v38diff` verified by zip central directory that the only differences are the vendor/ tree, reference_compile=false in the CE-1 config, the tokenizer_class fix, and run.py. The environment is the only moving part.
ruler: public LB
delta: v40 = 0.522171008743644 vs v39 = 0.5230454881 = -0.0008744794. THE ENVIRONMENT FIX COSTS POINTS. Decomposition of the two slots, and it closes exactly: CE-1 swap alone (v39-v30) +0.0013135348; runtime alone (v40-v39) -0.0008744794; both together (v40-v30) +0.0004390554, and the two legs sum to the joint to the last digit
notes: scope: THE VENDORED 4.57.3 RUNTIME AS SHIPPED IN v38/v40 -- the vendor tree plus reference_compile=false plus the tokenizer_class fix, applied to a ModernBERT/mmBERT CE-1 at 1024. It does NOT close the question of whether a rope-correct model TRAINED and TUNED end to end under 4.57.3 would do better; it closes shipping the corrected runtime under a model selected and a container fitted under 5.x. THE ROPE STORY WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE MECHANISM AND WRONG ABOUT THE VALUE. The bug is real and documented: the grader image runs transformers 5.14.1, which reads ModernBERT's rope config by the 5.x path and gives CE-1 a sliding theta of 160000 where training used 10000, scoring corr 0.9939 against the correct path. I described this as 'the champion's 0.5217320 is the score of a model running on the wrong RoPE theta'. That was accurate and it did not matter: correcting it moves the board DOWN by 0.00087. corr 0.9939 was always the tell -- the two runtimes agree on the overwhelming majority of the ranking, so the residual was never going to be worth much in either direction, and `envfixlocal`'s own CI95 [-0.00413, +0.01081] crossed zero. The board picked the negative half of that interval. IS IT NOISE? Partly, and this must be said. |0.00087| is 1.25x the UPPER bound of the determinism floor `receiptcensus` bracketed at [3e-05, 7e-04] and never measured. So the SIGN is not established beyond doubt; what IS established is that the fix is not worth a slot, because its entire effect lives at the scale of a floor we have never measured. WHAT THIS KILLS. (1) v38 -- the env fix alone on the v30 base -- is now pointless; it would score about 0.5209, below v30. Do not spend a slot on it. (2) It removes the last non-euro reason to carry the vendor tree at all: 2,530 files, +85 lines of run.py, for a board negative. (3) It raises the bar on euro-610m further, since euro CANNOT CONSTRUCT under 5.14.1 (`euroconstruct`, `v31resolved`) and therefore REQUIRES this runtime -- so any future euro container starts 0.00087 in the hole before the head is even considered, on top of v36's -0.0074. WHAT IT VINDICATES: `shiponevariable`. Two consecutive slots, one variable each, and the decomposition closes exactly. Had these been bundled into a single submission we would have read +0.00044 and learned nothing about either leg -- which is precisely what happened with v36, where the env fix and the euro head moved together and the result has been unreadable ever since. The human split them; the split is the reason both numbers mean something.

what: BOX DEATH #9 took BOTH boxes at once, mid-run, WITH NO MONITOR WATCHING. Recovery, plus four operational faults it exposed -- three of them mine, and one of them a repeat of a documented failure that has now cost GPU time twice.
ruler: none -- ops
delta: LOST: t175bal Stage B, about 50 GPU-minutes. SAVED: t175bal's Stage A, the 70-minute leg carrying the entire intervention, because push_ckpt pushed it to gordeevmax/ecup26-t175bal-stagea (573,198,684 B) at 13:32 before the box died. Also lost: ce_scores_t149baseA-ep1.npz, 25 GPU-minutes, rebuilt by queue93. The READINGS off that dump survive in `sbep1` and `confarm`, so no science was lost
notes: FAULT 1, MINE, AND THE EXPENSIVE ONE: ZERO MONITORS IS NOT THE FIX FOR TOO MANY MONITORS. Seventeen box_monitor processes were alive at once, fifteen of them still polling boxes dead for hours or days, and the operator asked for them to stop. I killed all seventeen and put nothing back. Both boxes died about ninety minutes later and nobody knew until the operator said so. The replacement is tools/box_sentry.py: ONE process, BOTH boxes, and it emits only on death, on QUEUE<n>_DONE, on a real failure signature, and one heartbeat an hour. No step counts, no MACRO lines, no stage transitions -- those were the spam. FAULT 2, MINE: restore_box.py IS NOT CONCURRENT AND NOTHING SAID SO. It calls box_bootstrap, which REWRITES the URL and TOKEN lines inside tools/box.py. I started it against both boxes at once; thirty seconds in, box.py pointed at Box B, and Box A's remaining uploads and its queue launch would have gone to Box B. Caught by reading box.py rather than by any error. Killed both, ran them serially. sync_boxes.py already does this the safe way -- per-box env vars, never a rewrite -- and box_sentry.py now follows it. FAULT 3, A REPEAT: push_ckpt.py WAS MISSING FROM THE BOX AGAIN. restore_box stalled around 116 of 140 files with the process still alive and its log silent, and the gap included push_ckpt.py -- the exact file whose absence on 2026-08-24 made every rolling checkpoint push fail and cost ~3.2 GPU-h. A partial bootstrap that LOOKS alive is as dangerous as a hand-rolled one. What caught it was a sha256 diff of the box against the canonical enumeration, not a file count. FIX, and it should be standing practice: after any bootstrap, diff the box against sorted(box/*.py + *.sh) BY HASH before launching anything. The gap was then closed with box_upload_slice.py, which exists for exactly this and shares the enumeration so a slice cannot silently omit a file. FAULT 4, IN MY OWN NEW TOOL, CAUGHT IN ITS FIRST MINUTE: the sentry alarmed immediately on a CUDA OOM from t165euroA2 and three flash-attn Tracebacks. None were current. /marimo IS A PERSISTENT VOLUME (`molabvolume`) -- it survives box death, so a BRAND-NEW box is handed every previous run's logs, and a naive tail of them reports history as news. The sentry now only considers files modified since it started. This is the second face of `molabvolume`: the volume surviving is usually the good news, and twice now it has also been the trap. WHAT WORKED, and it is the whole reason this was cheap: push-from-inside-the-trainer. `molabdies` says push checkpoints from the trainer, not from the queue script, and that is why the 70-minute Stage A was on Kaggle before the box went. The resume is FAITHFUL rather than approximate: under the shipped --sched-epochs 0, train_epoch builds a FRESH optimizer and a FRESH warmup->0 schedule every epoch and `convaudit` confirmed optimizer state is never saved, so Stage B from a Stage-A checkpoint IS the original recipe. The one real difference is that Stage A consumed random numbers, so the Stage-B batch order differs -- a SEED difference, inside the run-to-run band, and stated in queue92's header rather than hidden. A DURABILITY GAP STILL OPEN, named so someone closes it: CHECKPOINTS are pushed to Kaggle and survive every death; SCORE DUMPS are not pushed anywhere. They live on the box that made them plus whatever the local machine happened to pull. 41 ce_scores dumps sit on local disk; t149baseA-ep1 was not among them because it was made and read entirely on-box, so it died. Either pull dumps to local as they land, or push them as a Kaggle dataset.

notes: WHY THIS INSTEAD OF A BACKBONE SWAP, which is where I was heading until the operator pushed back and asked why we would re-run bge when all three of us have already mined it. The answer is in our own ledger and I had not read it: `mmbertread` PRE-REGISTERED A LENGTH STRATUM to split v24's +0.02255 into its two moving parts, and the split is lopsided -- the BACKBONE was worth +0.00229 and the rest was the WINDOW. That row's scope line says outright it 'kills mmBERT AS A BACKBONE REPLACEMENT for the CE-1 slot'. The window is spent (`windowsat`: 0.66% of pairs truncate at 1024 against 61.9% at 256), so ANOTHER BACKBONE AT THE SAME WINDOW BUYS ABOUT +0.002, not +0.02. `mmbertbench` adds that mmBERT is 5% SLOWER than bge at equal window, so the advertised 2-4x does not apply at our 340-token average either. Capacity is not the lever it looked like. WHAT THE LEDGER SAYS THE LEVER IS, in `stageavol`'s own words: 'SO THE INTERESTING AXIS IS MIX, NOT VOLUME.' We train at 55% positive; matches_llm's own distribution is 23/12/64; the board runs at ~4.5%. The ABUNDANT class is the under-used one -- we take 7.0% of the available zeros against 45.8% of the positives. AND MIX IS WHAT UNLOCKS VOLUME, which is the part neither row states. The pure-volume ceiling is only 2.18x BECAUSE the sampler holds a fixed 12:5:5 ratio and positives are the scarce class; `dose2x` already spent 2.0x of that, so volume-at-fixed-mix is 91% exhausted. Drop the positive share to the pool's own and the entire 11.19M becomes reachable. The two axes are COUPLED by construction, so this arm moves both on purpose -- separating them would mean not testing the thing. `shiponevariable` governs SLOTS, not training arms; t177vol is the control that splits them if this wins. SCALES SIT 0.002 UNDER THE EXACT RATIOS ON PURPOSE: the sampler ASSERTS on an over-draw rather than silently shrinking, and an assert at minute forty is a dead box life. IT WILL OUTLIVE A BOX AND THAT IS PLANNED FOR: --ckpt-every 1000 writes a rolling partial and push_ckpt ships Stage A to Kaggle the moment it completes, which is exactly what saved t175bal's 70-minute Stage A through box death #9 this afternoon. THE READ IS ONE-SIDED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS AXIS IS RUNNABLE AT ALL. `mixaxisclosed` (CLOSED-CONFIRMED) showed E_real gets the training-mix sign wrong at EVERY prevalence, tested against the v10/v6 board receipt. `stageavol2x` then worked out WHY, and why the error is ASYMMETRIC rather than random: E_real's real slice IS matches.parquet, i.e. the HUMAN distribution, so it flatters whichever arm leans human and penalises whichever leans LLM. More Stage A leans LLM. The bias therefore points in a KNOWN direction, which makes exactly one direction of the read sound: E_real says BETTER -> credible, because the gain had to overcome a bias working against it; E_real says WORSE -> UNINFORMATIVE, decides nothing. A one-sided instrument is not a broken one. PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE ANY NUMBER EXISTS: >= +0.006 E_real at the MATCHED ep0 comparison against t149baseA-ep0 -> ACCEPT and it earns a slot; anything else -> NO DECISION on the axis, and the checkpoint is kept only as a CE-1 artifact for the container comparison, which is artifact SELECTION and carries no mix-axis inference. E_mix and E_mined are DESCRIPTIVE ONLY here -- `eminediso` showed E_mix's delta IS its mined-negative component, and these arms change negative composition more than anything we have run.

what: A MOLAB SANDBOX CAN BE REPLACED IN PLACE, ON THE SAME URL, AND EVERY REACHABILITY CHECK WE HAVE STAYS GREEN THROUGH IT. Box B was swapped at 15:37 UTC while t176full was training. The operator noticed an idle GPU; the sentry had been silent for 45 minutes.
ruler: none -- ops
delta: Evidence, all from one probe: uptime -s = 15:37 against a run launched at 14:57; EVERY path in /marimo restamped 15:37; storage/, all 140 uploaded scripts, the 1,968 MB items_llm_subset.parquet, the access token and both logs GONE; and stale push-ecup26-wcat* directories from a previous box BACK. GPU 0%, 0 MiB. Cost: ~40 min of t176full and nothing else -- it had not yet reached its first rolling checkpoint
notes: THIS IS NOT THE BOX DEATH WE HAVE A MEMORY FOR. `molabdies` covers a sandbox that goes 410 Gone -- loud, and every tool notices. This one kept answering 200 with a valid session list the whole time, because a NEW sandbox had been placed behind the SAME URL. Reachability, session count, HTTP status and token validity were all unchanged and all wrong. AND THE VOLUME CAME BACK AS AN OLDER SNAPSHOT, which is the second face of `molabvolume` -- 'survival can also SILENTLY swap a run's inputs and cost you a lineage'. It is worse than an empty disk: the wcat directories from days ago reappeared, so a naive check for 'does /marimo look populated' would have passed. The only fields that moved were the boot time and the specific files we had put there. THE FIX, and it is one line of probe: box_sentry.py now reports `uptime -s` on every sweep and alarms REPLACED when it changes, separately from DOWN. Reachability is not liveness for a run; the sandbox identity is. It also clears its seen-set on a swap, because the new box's logs are a different history. WHAT SAVED THE REST, and it is worth stating because it is the design that keeps paying: train_ce.py:961 pushes the ROLLING MID-EPOCH partial off-box, not just to /marimo -- `push_off_box(f'{ckpt}/{tag}-partial', ...)` on every --ckpt-every interval. Kaggle already holds ecup26-t175bal-llm-ep0-partial and ecup26-t149basea-llm-ep0-partial as receipts. So a replacement costs at most CKPT_EVERY steps, roughly four minutes at 1000. t176full lost 40 minutes only because it had not reached step 1000 yet. The /marimo rolling checkpoint alone would have been worthless here, since /marimo is exactly what got swapped.

what: HOST RAM SCALES WITH PAIRS x DATALOADER WORKERS, and at t176full's 11,182,000-pair draw that product took the box to 899 MiB available with no swap. Caught because the operator asked why Box B was using only 2 GB of VRAM -- the VRAM was fine and beside the point; the host was one allocation from the OOM killer.
ruler: none -- ops
delta: MEASURED at step 5000/87359: free -h = 160Gi total, 159Gi used, AVAILABLE 899Mi, Swap 0B. Trainer RSS 36,360,916 kB (parent) + 32,234,312 kB (one worker) with six more behind it. AFTER dropping num_workers 8 -> 2 on the identical draw: 18Gi used, 141Gi AVAILABLE. Same pairs, same batch size, same window -- a 140 GB swing from one integer
notes: THE MECHANISM: DataLoader was hardcoded num_workers=8, persistent_workers=True at all three construction sites. Each worker is a FORK, and CPython's refcounter writes to the object header on every access, so copy-on-write degrades toward a REAL copy of whatever the parent holds. The tokenised set is ~32 GB at 11.18M pairs, so eight workers is ~9 copies. At the champion's 2.2M draw the same 8 workers are free -- this is why it has never bitten before and why it will bite every large-draw arm from now on. This is `oompattern` in a new place: that row was one object held twice, this is one object held nine times. WHY I RESTARTED INSTEAD OF LETTING IT FALL OVER. An OOM kill would have been survivable on its own -- the step-5000 partial was already on Kaggle with a full resume bundle. But --resume-partial would have rebuilt the SAME eight workers and died in the same place: an OOM LOOP that makes no progress and burns the box life. The configuration had to change, so paying ~35 minutes of text-build and length-bucketing was the cheap option. Zero training steps were lost. WORKERS ARE NOT THE BOTTLENECK HERE, which is why 2 is safe: nvidia-smi read 97% GPU utilisation before the restart, so the loader was already ahead of the GPU and the run is compute-bound. Pre-restart rate was 143 steps/min (steps 4000-5000 in 3.5 min); if the post-restart rate differs materially that is a finding in itself and the log will show it. A SECOND, SMALLER BUG IN MY OWN GUARD, recorded because it argued the wrong way. queue96's bundle check named `resume_meta.json`, which does not exist, so it emitted 'NOTE: absent -- resume will fall back to a fresh seam' about a PERFECTLY HEALTHY bundle, and the claim was wrong twice over: the real file is `train_state.json` (train_ce.py:570) and its absence causes a SystemExit, not a fallback. I nearly acted on my own false alarm; what settled it was reading the trainer's guard rather than trusting mine. The check is now fail-closed on the three files that actually matter -- train_state.json, batch_order.npz, rng_state.pt. GENERAL RULE FOR ANY ARM ABOVE ~4M PAIRS: pass --num-workers 2. The flag defaults to 8 so every existing recipe is byte-identical; only large draws need it. CORRECTION, 2026-08-29 18:2x -- THIS ROW OVERSTATED THE SAFETY NET AND THE CLAIM WAS CHECKABLE WHEN I MADE IT. Above I wrote that 'the step-5000 partial was already on Kaggle with a full resume bundle' and that 'Zero training steps were lost'. Both are FALSE. The restarted run printed 'llm-ep0: RESUME at step 1000/87359' and the bundle's train_state.json reads {'step': 1000}, so the durable resume point was step 1000 while the run had been observed at step 5000. About 4,000 steps -- ~28 min at the measured 143 steps/min, 4.6% of the epoch -- were lost, not zero. I asserted the checkpoint's contents from the value of --ckpt-every instead of reading train_state.json, which was one command away. THE BUNDLE ITSELF IS SOUND, and this is the part that matters for the run now in flight: all seven files carry mtimes 17:30:38-17:30:42 from a single download of ONE Kaggle push (created 17:01:49), so weights, batch order, RNG and step all come from the same instant. There is NO weights-vs-step mismatch, which was the failure worth fearing -- that would have replayed 4,000 batches onto weights that had already seen them, silently. The trainer's df_len/df_sig gate cannot catch that class of error, since it validates the DATA, not the weights. WHY THE DURABLE POINT LAGGED SO FAR: UNKNOWN, and I am not going to invent a mechanism. The original t176full.log was overwritten by the restart, so the push lines are gone. The one hypothesis that fits the timing -- slow uploads -- is REFUTED by measurement: the ancestor mirror pushed the same 616 MB at 18:13 in about 20 seconds. So pushes are fast and something else stopped them from firing or from landing. `kagglecli` (returncode is meaningless, exits 0 on 403s) is the obvious suspect and is exactly the failure mode that would leave no trace. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS RUN: --ckpt-every 1000 is currently believed to bound a box death's cost at 1000 steps. This run is a counterexample at 4,000, and `boxswap`'s claim that 'a replacement costs at most CKPT_EVERY steps, roughly four minutes' inherits the same overstatement -- flagged there rather than rewritten, since the row is otherwise sound. The cheap instrument is a log line naming the step and the dataset version on every completed push, so the durable lag is observable instead of reconstructed after the fact. Not built yet; both GPUs are busy and this run is healthy.

what: THE RESUME PATH WAS QUADRATIC IN PAIRS AND NOBODY COULD SEE IT. Rebuilding the batch list from batch_order.npz re-decompressed the ENTIRE index array once PER BATCH. At t176full's 11.18M-pair draw that is a 9.4-hour no-op between the last log line and the first training step, with the GPU at 0% the whole time.
ruler: none -- ops
delta: MEASURED on the box, not inferred. batch_order.npz is 43.6 MB on disk / 89.5 MB uncompressed (11,181,952 int64). Timed: first z['idx'] access 0.39 s, SECOND access 0.39 s, and `a is b` is False -- np.load returns a lazy NpzFile that caches nothing. n_batches = 87,359, so the comprehension costs 0.39 x 87,359 = 9.4 HOURS. Corroborated independently by /proc/<pid>/io: rchar 255,079,241,336 (255 GB of reads against a 43.6 MB file) and 3,975,073 read syscalls, with fd 39 held open on batch_order.npz for 29 minutes. Progress at detection: ~2,865 of 87,359 batches, i.e. 3.3% in 38 min. AFTER the one-line fix the same step is one decompression
artifacts: box/train_ce.py:843-857 (idx, sizes hoisted out of the comprehension), team/box_train_ce.py, sha256 bb75771b5d1520d5 verified on BOTH boxes
notes: THE BUG, exactly: `batches = [z['idx'][off[k]:off[k+1]].tolist() for k in range(len(z['sizes']))]`. `z` is an NpzFile, which is a handle on a ZIP -- every `z[key]` re-reads and re-inflates the whole member. The slice looks like cheap numpy indexing; the decompression is hidden inside __getitem__. Fix is to bind `idx, sizes = z['idx'], z['sizes']` once. WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG: the cost is O(n_batches x n_pairs), i.e. QUADRATIC in the draw. At the champion's 2.2M pairs it is ~17k batches x 17.6 MB ~ 20 minutes -- annoying, attributable to 'resumes are slow', and never questioned. At 5x the pairs it is 25x the cost and becomes longer than the training it precedes. Every large-draw arm from here would have paid it. WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, which is the transferable part: there is NO log line between 'train-seed=0' (train_ce.py:1106) and 'RESUME at step N/M' (:851). The whole resume reconstruction happens in that gap, so a stuck resume and a working one emit byte-identical logs. The tell was not the log at all -- it was GPU 0% while 19 CPU cores ran hot, which reads like tokenisation and is not. Reading /proc/<pid>/io and the open-fd list is what named the file; a stack dump would have been faster but py-spy cannot ptrace in this sandbox even under sudo. HOW IT WAS NEARLY MISSED. I had already written the wrong explanation into queue96's own header -- 'what is repaid is the text build and the length-bucketing pre-pass' -- and 29 silent minutes fit that story comfortably. It is false: train_ce.py:856 makes length_grouped_batches an `elif` on the resume branch, so a resume NEVER runs the pre-pass. Believing my own comment would have cost 9 hours of a 96 GB GPU. The check that broke it was reading the code path rather than the comment describing it -- the same move that settled the resume_meta.json false alarm in `workermem` a few hours earlier, which is twice in one day that my own documentation argued against the source. COST AND CREDIT: ~38 min of Box B, and the step-5000 partial was untouched, so zero training steps were lost -- the rolling off-box checkpoint (`boxswap`) covered this exactly as designed. Box A's t177vol is NOT affected: it is a fresh run, so it builds batches in memory via length_grouped_batches and never touches this path. Both boxes now carry the patched trainer anyway, because the next resume is always one box death away.

One runtime (4.57.3), one weight set (t167llm2x-ep1, the shipped CE-1), 96 real human pairs, only local_rope_theta moving. pearson 0.990869 | spearman 0.990057 | mean |diff| 0.031596 | max |diff| 0.232384 | 87 OF 96 PAIRS CHANGE RANK. THE RE-ATTRIBUTION, which is the real content of this row. v39 and v40 run the same weights on the same pairs through two transformers versions that compute the SAME OPERATIONS; the one numerically material difference between them is local rope theta (160000 vs 10000). So v40's -0.00087 is best read not as the price of 'the environment fix' but as THE BOARD PRICE OF THE ROPE CORRECTION ITSELF. `v40lb` named the wrong active variable. AND THAT KILLS THE LEVER RATHER THAN OPENING IT. what: A FRESH SANDBOX SERVED A STALE TRAINING INPUT AND ONLY THE PREFLIGHT NOTICED. Box B came back from death #11 with /marimo carrying an items_llm_subset.parquet from an OLDER, SMALLER draw. queue98 guarded on `[ ! -s file ]` -- presence, not validity -- so it skipped the rebuild and handed the trainer the wrong subset.
ruler: none -- ops
delta: Stale file 539,488,868 B, mtime = the new box's boot time; the full-pool draw needs 1,968,262,613 B. preflight_draw.py: 'unique items needed 12379530, subset has 3304398, MISSING 9075132 -> COVERAGE_BAD'. 73% of the items the draw requires were absent. Caught BEFORE a single training step
notes: THIS IS `molabvolume`'s SECOND FACE, the one that is worse than an empty disk: the volume SURVIVES and silently swaps a run's inputs. An empty /marimo is loud -- every guard fires. A /marimo repopulated with last week's artifacts is silent, and a presence check passes it. `boxswap` recorded the same shape (stale push-ecup26-wcat* dirs reappearing); this is the first time it reached a TRAINING INPUT rather than scratch files. WHY NOTHING WAS LOST: preflight_draw.py runs between the subset and the trainer and emits COVERAGE_OK/COVERAGE_BAD, and queue98 greps for it. Had that gate not existed, t176full would have resumed from step 57000 onto a draw missing 9.07M items -- and it would NOT have crashed, it would have trained a dose-confounded arm to completion and the number would have entered the ledger looking clean. Note the trainer's own df_len/df_sig guard would ALSO not have caught it: it validates the pair table against the resume bundle, not the item subset those pairs are drawn from. Two independent guards, only one of them covers this. THE FIX, and the general rule: PRESENCE IS NOT VALIDITY. queue98 now runs the preflight FIRST, rebuilds only when it fails, and re-runs it after the rebuild as a binding gate. Any guard of the form `[ -s file ] && skip_expensive_rebuild` on a persistent volume is the same bug waiting to happen -- the check has to be on CONTENT (coverage, signature, size against the expected draw), never on existence. COST: zero training, ~2 minutes of preflight, and the rebuild that should have run anyway.

what: Task-vector geometry of the same-ancestor mmBERT-base family (t126mmB-ep1, t136sa-ep1, t167llm2x-ep1, t177vol-ep1) against W_base = jhu-clsp/mmBERT-base. Asks whether the five weight-soup rejections are explained by head mis-alignment or by sign interference.
ruler: direct weight/task-vector measurement (tools/ties_merge.py geometry probe); no ruler, no GPU
delta: heads ALIGNED: classifier.weight cos +0.995..+0.99992, head.norm cos +1.00000. raw weights NEAR-IDENTICAL: cos +0.998..+1.000, ||A-B||/||A|| 0.0005..0.06. TASK VECTORS DIVERSE: cos(tau) +0.35..+0.92; sign-conflict 9.6..28.4%; layers.21.mlp.Wo 2-2 tied on 14.0% of parameters
notes: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT REFUTED MY OWN HYPOTHESIS. I predicted the five soup rejections were caused by mis-aligned classifier heads (different random init per run -> averaging is noise). That is FALSE here: classifier.weight cos +0.995..+0.99992, head.norm.weight cos +1.00000 to five places across all six pairs. The heads are aligned, so weight merging is geometrically legitimate in this family and the five rejections need a different explanation. THE RAW WEIGHTS ARE A RED HERRING. Pairwise ||A-B||/||A|| is 0.0005..0.06 and cos is +0.998..+1.000 on every tensor probed, which reads as 'these are the same model'. They are not: ||tau|| = ||W_i - W_base|| is only 1.2..4.2% of ||W_base||, so the four checkpoints share 96-99% of their mass with the pretrain and differ ONLY inside that thin learned shell. Comparing W to W hides the entire signal; comparing tau to tau exposes it. WHAT THE TASK VECTORS ACTUALLY SAY: layers.21.mlp.Wo cos(tau) +0.6215..+0.7815, sign-conflict 21.0..28.4%, 4-way split unanimous 53.7% / 3-1 32.3% / 2-2 TIED 14.0%. head.dense cos(tau) +0.8030..+0.9220, conflict 13.5..18.5%, tied 9.1%. tok_embeddings cos(tau) +0.3523..+0.4552, conflict 9.6..11.0%, tied 6.8%. THE MECHANISM THIS EXPOSES: a uniform average of weights is an average of task vectors, and at a 2-2 split the average is ~ZERO -- it does not pick a winner, it DELETES a feature that both models learned. 14.0% of the MLP output projection is in that state. That is textbook sign interference and it is a specific, testable cause for `soupbge` -0.00200 / `xsoupgv` -0.00454 / `soupdesync` REJECT, none of which tested a fix for it. ORDERING NOTE: t126mmB-ep1 is the outlier of the four (cos(tau) ~0.62 against the others, ||tau|| 4.2% vs 2.5-2.9%), consistent with it being the oldest member. DOES NOT LICENSE MERGING ACROSS BACKBONES: euro and bge have different W_base and different shapes; this row is about the mmBERT-base family only.

what: TIES-Merging and SLERP over the same-ancestor mmBERT-base family, as a CE-1 replacement. Four arms: TIES(3, lambda 1.0), TIES(3, lambda 1.3), SLERP(A,C,t=0.5), TIES(4, lambda 1.0). Reopens the 0-for-5 weight-merging axis on the strength of the `tiesgeom` mechanism.

Reopening on a measured mechanism rather than on hope is the `gatesthatonlykill` rule. The operator also explicitly asked for this axis to be revisited after I raised the 0-for-5 record. what: How run.py behaves when a CE stage overruns: FORCE_CE=1 makes every in-container 'skip if short on budget' check inert, and a timeout in ANY cross-encoder discards ALL CE scores and ships the GBDT alone. Found while attempting to validate a CE-3 stage in the grader image.
ruler: direct observation in twirlz/ecup26-matching:1.0 on the 11,000-pair labelled repro set (no ruler delta)
delta: 3-CE archive: watchdog fired at 334s inside CE-1, 'cross-encoder failed ... GBDT result retained', done in 370s against a 360s stage budget. Same CE-1 completed within a 251s total v41 run on the same GPU earlier the same day
notes: scope: the container's TIME-SAFETY behaviour, learned while trying to validate a CE-3 stage. No ruler delta -- this is a mechanism finding about run.py, and it applies to ANY future change that adds inference work. TWO THINGS I ASSERTED THIS MORNING THAT ARE WRONG. (1) I said a third CE 'fails safe by skipping'. It does not, in the shipped configuration: run.py line 151 sets force_ce = os.environ.get("FORCE_CE", "1") == "1" and n > 10_000, and line 154 sets deadline_ts = None if force_ce else ..., so with the DEFAULT FORCE_CE=1 on any scored stage the deadline is None, every `left = deadline_ts - time.time()` becomes 1e9, and the 'SKIP if short on budget' branches in CE-2 AND in a CE-3 are INERT. They never fire. The only real limit is the SIGALRM cap at T0 + total_budget*0.97. (2) I said the downside was bounded at parity with v39. The observed failure mode is worse than that: the alarm raised TimeoutError INSIDE CE-1's forward pass, it propagated to the OUTER `except Exception as exc` around the whole CE section, and the log reads 'ERROR: cross-encoder failed (TimeoutError(...)); GBDT result retained'. A timeout ANYWHERE in the CE block discards EVERY cross-encoder score and ships the GBDT alone -- the v37 class of outcome (0.3611536), not parity. A per-stage try/except (which the CE-3 patch does have) protects only overruns raised INSIDE its own stage. MEASURED, on an 11,000-pair labelled set in twirlz/ecup26-matching:1.0 on a local RTX 3050: the 3-CE archive hit the watchdog at 334s and finished at 370s against a 360s stage budget. THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY FOR TIMING AND I AM SAYING SO PLAINLY: the SAME CE-1, in the SAME image, on the SAME GPU, completed inside a 251s total run for v41 earlier the same day. A stage that varies from 'part of 251s' to 'blew 334s' between runs cannot price a +9% workload increase. So this row does NOT establish that a third CE is unaffordable on the grader's H100; it establishes what HAPPENS if any stage overruns, which is the part that was mis-stated. RELATED, AND THE REASON THE COST ARITHMETIC KEEPS MISLEADING US: `bench_infer.py`'s own header says it cannot measure the H100-vs-RTX-6000 gap, and every CE-minute figure in this repo descends from it. That model prices the CHAMPION at 2.76 + 9.44 + 1.24 = 13.44 min against a 13.0 budget -- it says v39 should NOT fit, while v39 scored 0.5230454881 on both splits. Any future 'X does not fit' claim must cite a measurement on grader-class hardware or be treated as unsupported. WHAT TO DO WITH A TIMING-INCREASING CHANGE IN FUTURE: run it in the image on a card that can complete the BASELINE comfortably, and read the delta between baseline and candidate on that SAME machine in the same session -- never the absolute number, and never against a budget the test machine cannot meet even for the unmodified champion.
